variables.name: Host Group
variables.input:
// Same sweep as the blog query, with status, target version, host and name added. Row count should match the blog query.
smartscapeNodes "PROCESS"
| fieldsAdd technologies = arrayConcat(process.software_technologies.php, process.software_technologies.os)
| expand technologies
| filter technologies[type] == "PHP"
| fieldsAdd php_version = if(isNotNull(technologies[version]) and technologies[version] != "", technologies[version])
| summarize php_version = takeAny(php_version), name = takeAny(name), host.name = takeAny(host.name),
            exe = takeAny(process.metadata[EXE_NAME]),
            public_traffic = if(takeAny(process.has_public_traffic) == true, "CONFIRMED", else: "NOT_CONFIRMED"),
            by: {id}
| parse php_version, "INT:major '.' INT:minor ('.' INT:patch)?"
| fieldsAdd patch = coalesce(patch, 0)
| fieldsAdd status = if(isNull(major), "UNKNOWN VERSION - CHECK",
    else: if(major < 7 or (major == 7 and minor < 4), "EOL - NO FIX",
    else: if(major < 8 or (major == 8 and minor < 2), "EOL - COMMUNITY BACKPORT ONLY",
    else: if((minor == 2 and patch < 35) or (minor == 3 and patch < 36)
          or (minor == 4 and patch < 27) or (minor == 5 and patch < 12), "VULNERABLE - PATCH AVAILABLE",
    else: "PATCHED"))))
| fieldsAdd fixed_in = if(major == 8 and minor == 2, "8.2.35",
    else: if(major == 8 and minor == 3, "8.3.36",
    else: if(major == 8 and minor == 4, "8.4.27",
    else: if(major == 8 and minor == 5, "8.5.12", else: "-"))))
| filter status != "PATCHED"
| fieldsAdd processId = toString(id)
| join [
  smartscapeNodes "PROCESS"
  | fieldsAdd technologies = arrayConcat(process.software_technologies.php, process.software_technologies.os)
  | expand technologies
  | filter technologies[type] == "PHP"
  | fieldsAdd php_version = if(isNotNull(technologies[version]) and technologies[version] != "", technologies[version])
  | fieldsAdd processId = toString(id)
], on:{processId}, kind:{inner}, prefix:"pgi.details."
| fieldsRename tags = pgi.details.tags
| fieldsRename host.group = pgi.details.dt.host_group.id
| summarize count=count(), by:{host.group} 
| fields host.group
| sort host.group asc

1.content:
## PHP2Shell exposure (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619)

*Fix*: PHP 8.5.12 · 8.4.27 · 8.3.36 · 8.2.35, or your distribution's patched package. Rebuild container images. **7.4–8.1:** apply the PHP team's source patches or a vendor backport and rebuild. **Below 7.4:** no fix; isolate or migrate. Updating is the only complete fix; interim hardening (`memory_limit`, `session.upload_progress.enabled=0`, `pm.max_requests=1`, low `post_max_size`) reduces but does not remove exposure.

*Reading this page.* Inventory comes from the PHP version OneAgent detects on each process, via Smartscape. **CONFIRMED public traffic** means Dynatrace has seen requests from the public internet reach the process; patch those first. Distro vendors may backport a fix without bumping the version string: confirm with `rpm -q` / `dpkg -l` before closing a finding. A process upgraded on disk but not restarted still shows the old version, which is correct: it is still exposed.

**Guidance:** [Dynatrace blog: PHP2Shell, what it is and what to do](https://www.dynatrace.com/news/blog/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619-php2shell-critical-vulnerability-what-it-is-and-what-to-do/)

12.content:
### Signs of attempted exploitation

The exploit must drive a PHP worker out of memory (or into a fatal error / timeout) before it can corrupt state. A spike in these log lines on a web tier that was flat last week is the attempt signature, including failed attempts. They do **not** confirm exploitation on their own. Pair with Davis problems on the same processes, and, where process-execution logs are collected, with shells or recon commands (`whoami`, `id`, `uname`) spawned by `apache2`, `nginx`, `php`, or `php-fpm` parents.

*Note*: given the urgency of this issue, the query scans below are using `5000 GiB` rather than the default of `500 GiB`. Use with caution.

13.title: Exploit-precondition log indicators per host (15m)
13.query:
// Log indicators (rebuilt from the Dynatrace PHP2Shell blog). These suggest attempts; they do not confirm exploitation.
fetch logs
| filter matchesValue(content, "*Allowed memory size of*")
      or matchesValue(content, "*Maximum execution time*")
      or matchesValue(content, "*exit signal Segmentation fault*")
      or matchesValue(content, "*exited on signal 11*")
      or matchesValue(content, "*PHP Fatal error*")
| makeTimeseries indicators = count(), by: {host.name}, interval: 15m

14.title: Indicators by host and type

16.title: Davis events on PHP and Apache processes (memory, crash, timeout)
16.query:
fetch dt.davis.events
| filter affected_entity_types == array("dt.entity.process_group_instance")
| filter contains(event.name, "Memory", caseSensitive:false) OR
contains(event.name, "Crash", caseSensitive:false) OR
contains(event.name, "Timeout", caseSensitive:false) OR
contains(event.name, "Unavailable", caseSensitive:false)
| expand affected_entity_ids
| fieldsAdd entity_id = toString(affected_entity_ids)
| join [fetch dt.entity.process_group_instance
| fieldsAdd id, entity.name], on:{left[entity_id]==right[id]}, kind:{inner}, prefix:"pgi."
| fields timestamp, display_id, event.name, event.status, affected_entity_ids, root_cause_entity_name, affected_entity_types, `Process`=pgi.entity.name
| filter contains(`Process`,"php", caseSensitive:false) OR contains(`Process`,"apache", caseSensitive:false)
| sort timestamp desc

17.content:
### What this page cannot see
PHP on hosts without OneAgent (agency-hosted sites, appliances, ops tooling). `php-cgi.exe` under IIS that OneAgent did not fingerprint as PHP. IIS sites with a `*.php` handler mapped but idle. Runtime Application Protection does not block this class of bug; Runtime Vulnerability Analytics covers libraries, not the PHP runtime, so this inventory is the source of truth.
